title: The Marīnids declare war on Gharnāṭa itself, demanding its submission as their subject, with Tilimsān, Tāfīlālt and Tuwāt beside them. Qashtāla takes the field to defend its tributary, and Portugal with it. It comes a year before the court meant to seek the Marīnids' alliance for a war of independence, and with relations between the two courts at their warmest
source: save of 26 June 1360; Trent's screenshot and account

title: Granadan sovereignty reaches 100, the full measure; influence −3.1, tipping just toward Qashtāla

The court's bitterness: Qashtāla and Portugal had bled in Arghūn (their losses reckoned at 10,000 and 30,000) and lay open to a war of independence. Instead Gharnāṭa must spend its own men throwing back the Marīnids until Qashtāla can send its levies south

The Dīwān al-Mustakhlaṣ is founded to administer the sultan's private domain, the estates, mills and revenues set apart from the public treasury to fund the court and al-Ḥamrāʾ. A new bureaucracy grows from the harem's widening influence, in the middle of the Marīnid war
source: Trent's screenshot of the bureaucracy choice and his account
